L:powerlines:8: ## If the forklift touches a powerline — the 5 steps
L:powerlines:10: 1. **STAY on the forklift.** Stay calm, stay seated and don't touch any metal parts. The forklift may be live — the ground around it can be too.
L:powerlines:11: 2. **WARN others.** Shout to everyone to keep **at least 8 metres** away. No one should touch the forklift or try to help you.
L:powerlines:12: 3. **BREAK contact — only if it's safe.** Lower the mast or tynes, or drive the forklift clear of the line, but only if it won't cause another hazard.
L:powerlines:13: 4. **CALL for help.** Call **000** and the local electricity network operator (e.g. Ausgrid 13 13 88, Endeavour Energy 13 10 03, Essential Energy 13 20 80) and ask them to switch the power off. **Stay where you are** until they confirm the power is off.
L:powerlines:14: 5. **JUMP clear — only if you must** (e.g. the forklift is on fire). Jump well clear with your **feet together**, never touching the forklift and the ground at the same time. Land with feet together, then **shuffle or bunny-hop** with feet together until you are **at least 8 metres** away. **Never go back** until the power is confirmed off.
L:powerlines:16: - Don't use the forklift again until it has been **inspected**.
L:powerlines:17: - Report it to your supervisor straight away. Contact with a powerline is a **notifiable incident** — your employer must notify the WHS regulator.
L:powerlines:18: > If you see someone else's machine touching a line: **stay back at least 8 m**, call 000 and the network operator, and tell them to stay on the machine.
L:ground-and-weather:1: A loaded forklift is extremely heavy — the counterweight alone can weigh more than the load. Check the surface can take it.
L:ground-and-weather:2:
| Surface | Risk / what to do |
|---|---|
| **Backfilled ground** (e.g. over a trench) | May collapse — avoid unless confirmed compacted and suitable |
| **Soft soil, mud, sand** | Wheels sink, forklift can tip — avoid or use suitable equipment |
| **Hard compacted soil** | Usually OK, but check after rain |
| **Damaged or cracked concrete / bitumen, potholes** | Jolts the load and forklift — slow down, go around, report |
| **Railway tracks** | Cross slowly and at an angle where possible so wheels don't drop into the gap |
| **Rough or sloped terrain** | Instability — slow down, keep the load low, follow ramp rules |
| **Steel decks, grates, trench covers, dock plates** | Must be rated for the **combined weight** of forklift and load, and secured |
L:ground-and-weather:4:
| Condition | Response |
|---|---|
| **Strong wind** | Large flat loads (sheet material, boards) act like a sail — slow down or stop work if unsafe |
| **Lightning** | Stop outdoor work, park safely and take shelter |
| **Rain, wet or icy surfaces** | Reduce speed, brake and turn gently, allow much longer stopping distances |
| **Extreme heat** | Drink water, take breaks, watch for heat stress; watch engine temperature |
| **UV exposure** | Sun protection — hat, long sleeves, sunscreen, sunglasses |
L:ground-and-weather:5: If conditions make the job unsafe, **stop and tell your supervisor**.
T:traffic-management-exclusion-zones: Traffic management plans and exclusion zones
L:traffic-management-exclusion-zones:1: Workplaces where forklifts operate should have a **traffic management plan (TMP)**. It typically sets out:
L:traffic-management-exclusion-zones:2: - **forklift routes** and **pedestrian walkways**, separated where possible
L:traffic-management-exclusion-zones:6: - **signage**, line marking, mirrors and warning lights
L:traffic-management-exclusion-zones:7: - rules for visitors and delivery drivers
L:traffic-management-exclusion-zones:8: Know the TMP for your site and **follow it every time**.
L:traffic-management-exclusion-zones:10: An **exclusion zone** is an area around forklift work that people must not enter. Set one up with **barriers, bollards, cones, bunting and signs** — for example while loading a truck or stacking at height.
L:traffic-management-exclusion-zones:11: - Check the zone is in place before you start.
L:traffic-management-exclusion-zones:13: - If a control is missing or damaged (a broken barrier, a faded walkway, a mirror knocked out of position), **report it** to your supervisor.
L:pre-start-checks:1: Carry out a pre-start check **before every shift**, using the site checklist and the operator's manual. With the engine **off**, walk around and check:
L:pre-start-checks:2: - **Data plate** — present, legible, and **correct for the attachment fitted**
L:pre-start-checks:3: - **Structure** — look for **cracked or stressed welds** and **paint separation** (cracked or flaking paint at joints can show a crack underneath)
L:pre-start-checks:4: - **Tynes (forks) / attachments** — cracks, bends, heel wear; **locking pins in place** and attachments **secure**
L:pre-start-checks:5: - **Mast, chains and carriage** — damage, wear, chain tension
L:pre-start-checks:6: - **Hydraulics** — hoses, fittings and the ground underneath for **leaks**
L:pre-start-checks:7: - **Fluids** — engine oil, hydraulic oil, coolant, **fuel / LPG level**
L:pre-start-checks:8: - **Battery** (electric) — **charge level**, cables and connectors, no damage
L:pre-start-checks:9: - **Tyres and wheels** — damage, wear, **correct inflation**, wheel nuts
L:pre-start-checks:10: - **Overhead guard and load backrest** — fitted and undamaged
L:pre-start-checks:11: - **Lights, safety equipment** (e.g. fire extinguisher if fitted) and **signs and labels** — present and legible
L:pre-start-checks:12: - **Logbook / checklist** — available, and previous defects followed up
L:pre-start-checks:14: Use the steps and handholds and keep **three points of contact** (two hands and a foot, or two feet and a hand). Never jump down.
L:pre-start-checks:15: Once seated, **adjust the seat and mirrors** and **fasten and test the seatbelt**.
L:pre-start-checks:16: Record the check, and **record any damage** you find.
T:operational-checks-and-defects: Operational checks and lock out / tag out
L:operational-checks-and-defects:1: Start the forklift **as the manufacturer requires** and check:
L:operational-checks-and-defects:8: - **Hydraulics** — run lift, tilt and side shift through their **full range**; movement should be smooth
L:operational-checks-and-defects:11: Record the results on the checklist.
L:operational-checks-and-defects:13: If you find a fault, the forklift must not be used until it's fixed:
L:operational-checks-and-defects:15: 2. **Isolate** the power — turn off, remove the key, close the LPG valve or disconnect the battery as your procedure says.
L:operational-checks-and-defects:16: 3. **Tag** it — attach an "Out of service / Do not operate" tag (and a lock if your site uses them).
L:operational-checks-and-defects:17: 4. **Report** the fault to your supervisor and record it.
L:operational-checks-and-defects:18: Only an **authorised person** may remove the tag, once the repair is done and checked.
L:faults-failures-routine-problems:1:
| Failure | What to do |
|---|---|
| **Brake failure** | Take your foot off the accelerator, **warn others with the horn**, steer away from people and obstacles, and use the park brake to bring the forklift to a stop. Lower the load. Tag out and report. |
| **Steering failure** | Stop as quickly and safely as you can, warn others, lower the load. Tag out and report. |
| **Hydraulic failure** (load drops or won't hold) | Keep everyone clear of the load, stop, lower it if you can. Tag out and report. |
| **Forklift starts to tip** | **Do not jump.** Stay in the seat with the seatbelt on, hold the steering wheel firmly, brace your feet and **lean away** from the direction of the fall. |
L:faults-failures-routine-problems:2: Equipment failure on a ramp, at height or near people is very dangerous — which is why pre-start and operational checks matter.
L:faults-failures-routine-problems:4:
| Sign | Likely cause | Correction |
|---|---|---|
| Engine stutters / loses power (LPG) | Cylinder running empty | Park safely, change the cylinder following the procedure |
| Battery indicator low | Battery discharged | Return to the charging area; charge or swap |
| Hydraulics slow or jerky | Low hydraulic oil or a leak | Check the level per the manual; if leaking, **tag out** and report |
| Temperature gauge high | Overheating | Stop, shut down, let it cool — never open a hot radiator cap. Report it. |
| Light, horn or alarm not working | Globe, fuse or fault | Report it — don't operate until fixed |
| Tyre looks low or damaged | Puncture / wear | Report — repairs by a competent person only |
L:faults-failures-routine-problems:5: Only fix problems that are **within your competence** and allowed by your workplace procedures. Everything else: tag out and report.
T:stability-triangle: Centre of gravity and the stability triangle
L:stability-triangle:0: ## How a counterbalance forklift stays upright
L:stability-triangle:1: A counterbalance forklift works like a **see-saw**: the front wheels are the pivot (fulcrum), the load is on one side and the counterweight on the other.
L:stability-triangle:2: Most counterbalance forklifts have **three-point suspension**: the two front wheels and the pivot point of the rear axle. These form the **stability triangle**.
